questions: Where A1c is between 5.7 and 6.4 with no diabetes diagnosis and no medication - here 5.9 - does house practice rate it purely on the section 6 table and the preferred-class thresholds (zero debits, Preferred still available at 6.0 or under), or is an undiagnosed A1c in that range on its own a reason to cap the class or add debits?

Section 16 refers 'combinations of cardiac risk factors' to judgement without saying what counts as one. On this file total cholesterol 211 (ratio 4.1) and A1c 5.9 each sit inside their zero-debit bands. Does the house treat two zero-debit markers like these as a combination that needs judgement, or does that referral only arise when at least one factor is already carrying a debit?
